question.text: Ferdinand and his wife were assassinated by this 19-year old Yugoslav nationalist. He was a member of the Black Hand, which planned Franz Ferdinand's assassination.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.text: This second-longest river of Europe begins in the Black Forest of Germany.
swap.clue: Despite not being native to it, the Phanariotes served as administrators of a region on this river.

question.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
question.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.text: This former president of Yugoslavia was put on trial for crimes against humanity, but he died during the proceedings at the Hague. He allegedly committed genocide in Kosovo.
swap.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

question.text: Apocryphally, the League of Nations offered English athlete C. B. Fry the vacant throne of this country after the First World War, but he declined. This country was instead ruled from 1928 to 1939 by its only king, Zog.
question.clue: Its King Zog was deposed by Mussolini, who attempted to invade Greece from this country, and it was formerly ruled by the communist dictator Enver Hoxha ("ho-sha").

swap.text: The newest member of the EU is this country which joined in 2013. Its leader, Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic works in its Presidential palace at Zagreb.
swap.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

question.leadin: In this leader's last public appearance, people shouted "Timisoara" in reference to an uprising he had violently suppressed.
question.text: Name this long-time Communist leader of Romania. This man and his wife's execution was nearly caught on live television following a 1989 revolution.
question.clue: In an effort to increase his country's population, he outlawed almost all forms ofcontraception in Decree 770, and he employed a secret police known as the Securitate.

swap.leadin: This man formed the Non-Aligned Movement with Nasser and Nehru.
swap.text: Identify this man who led his country to become the only member of Cominform to repel Soviet domination.
swap.clue: This leader was excommunicated after convicting Archbishop Aloysius Stepinac for his involvement with the Ustase.

question.text: Out With The Old Founded in the fourteenth century as Dambovita Citadel, this key city along the trade route to Constantinople became the residence of the Walachian prince. The home of the headquarters of Cominform from 1948 to 1956, much of its Old City was demolished for new buildings on a tributary of the Danube. For 15 points-name this Eastern European city.
question.clue: A coup led by this city's orthodox Metropolitan Neophyte ended its post-1848 revolutionary period.

swap.leadin: The early rulers of these people, including Asparukh, are listed in the Nominalia.
swap.text: Name these people who were soundly defeated at the Battle of Kleidion by Basil II, who was nicknamed the "Slayer" of these people.
swap.clue: Many members of this ethnicity were killed by bashi-bazouk (BYE-jee-buh-ZOOK) soldiers during the April Uprising in namesake "horrors."

question.leadin: Ante Pavelic served as the Poglavnik of this organization from 1941 to 1945.
question.text: Name this fascist organization that ruled a Nazi puppet state from Zagreb. One member of this organization was known for keeping a jar of eyeballs on his desk.
question.answerHtml: Ustaše (us-TA-shay) [accept but do NOT otherwise reveal Ustaša (us-TA-sha) – Croatian Revolutionary Movement; accept but do Not otherwise reveal Ustaša – Hrvatski revolucionarni pokret; do NOT accept or prompt on “Croatia”]
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the military successes and failures of the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: The Ottoman sultan Murad II defeated the "Athlete of Christ," Janos Hunyadi, at the battle of Varna in this country. Basil II earned one of his epithets by subjugating this country.
swap.clue: One leader of this nation was ousted after members of the NGO Ecoglasnost were beaten by the police, leading to the one-year term of Petar Mladenov.

question.text: This 1878 settlement of the Russo-Turkish War created several new Slavic states with autonomy from the Ottoman Empire, but it was modified at the Congress of Berlin after Bismarck found it upsetting to the balance of power.
question.clue: This 1878 treaty, which ended the Russo-Turkish War and was softened at the Berlin Congress, recognized the independenece of Serbia, Montenegro, Romania, and Bulgaria.

swap.text: In the 1880s, Austria-Hungary used this city's tramways as testing grounds for trams to be used in Vienna. This city was the site of the Markale ("mar-KAH-leh") massacres during a 1992 to 1996 siege involving the JNA.
swap.answerHtml: Sarajevo [accept Siege of Sarajevo; accept Romeo and Juliet in Sarajevo]
swap.clue: This city contains the Latin Bridge, the site of a notable assassination.

question.leadin: After forcing King Carol II to abdicate, this man declared a "National Legionary State."
question.text: Name this conducator who forged a pro-German military dictatorship in his country through a coalition with Horia Sima and the paramilitary Iron Guard.
question.clue: He was the first non-monarch in his country to call himself the "Conducator."

swap.leadin: This country's war of independence began a year after the Log Revolution and included the Vukovar massacre.
swap.text: Name this country that carried out Operation Storm, resulting in the defeat of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.
swap.clue: During World War II, this country was ruled by Ante Pavlevic and his fascist Ustasa, which conducted a massive ethnic cleansing campaign in areas like Slavonia and Krajina.

question.text: Along with Milosevic, this neofascist Croatian dictator was party to the earlier 1995 Dayton Accords, which allowed for the NATO implementation force to take over for U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia.
question.clue: This president of Croatia throughout most of the 1990s. He signed the Erdut Agreement with the remaining independent republics and thus fully achieved Croatian independence.

swap.text: Peter's monarchy was destroyed by this leader of the Partisans and Cominform in Yugoslavia, who served as its dictator all the way through to 1980.
swap.clue: With the help of his secret police, the UDBA, this man ruled through the Informbiro schism as the leader of Yugoslavia from World War II until 1980.

question.text: NATO attacked Yugoslavia after the failure of this 1999 treaty, which granted temporary autonomy to Kosovo.

swap.leadin: In 1947, this leader signed the Bled Agreement with Josip Tito in an attempt to realize a Balkan Federation with Yugoslavia, although it never came to fruition.
swap.text: Name this leader, whose eponymous constitution replaced one named for the city of Veliko Tarnovo. This man and two fellow Comintern agents had earlier been acquitted in Leipzig for their role in the 1933 Reichstag fire.
swap.answerHtml: Georgi Dimitrov [or Georgi Dimitrov Mihaylov or Georgiy Mihaylovich Dimitrov]
